_what: The screen a person's words pick as they type, before any AI answers (src/instant-screens.mjs, drawn under the message box by src/workspace/instant-screen.tsx). Every screen the person is offered is a candidate (the app's screens, every tool's own screen, a Marketplace tool they installed, a screen an AI saved for them), and so is every interface of controls an AI made (its intent) and every screen the person kept from here (their words). `fields` is how much a word counts where it is found: in the words that asked for the screen (`asked`: a saved screen's `screen.asked`, a made interface's intent, a kept screen's words), its name (`label`) or its line about what it does (`about`). `match` is how much a typed word counts for each kind of likeness: the same word, the start of a word (the word being typed), or a word one or two letters away (a slip); the start of a word counts from `starts_letters` letters, so two letters typed never pick a screen by a guess. `label_cover` lifts a screen whose name the words say all of. `decide` is how calm the answer stays: a pick shows at `show_at`, a different screen replaces the one shown only after winning `challenger_wins` times in a row (or at once at `challenger_override`), the one shown goes when its own share falls below `drop_below` and nothing reaches `show_at`, and a screen the person chose stays until the words change by more than `forced_change` of their length. `remembered_answers` is how many typed words keep their answer on this page (the oldest let go first); `candidates_max` bounds how many screens one keystroke weighs. `debounce_ms` is how long the words must rest before anything leaves the device for them (the screen's description, the optional fill); the pick itself is made on this device at once. `swap_after_ms` is the longest a newly picked screen is drawn out of sight before it replaces the one shown, if it has not finished drawing by then. `fill.provider` names an optional tool that fills inputs the parsers could not (a Workshop tool id, run like any tool: given { words, schema }, answering { values }); null asks nothing. `fill.timeout_ms` is how long it may take before the parsed values stand alone; it is never tried again. `asks` is where the person's kept screens are kept (a workspace preference) and how many. `words` are every word the box's answer says.

words.label: A screen for what you typed
